page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Compute is delivered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz across 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with symmetric multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per-core allocation. Storage is provided directly as 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the server features a 20 Gbps baseline network throughput. The hardware configuration contains no GPUs.

Benchmark results display distinct performance characteristics between single-threaded and parallel execution. Single-core tests reflect lower relative execution speed, recording 726.0 in Geekbench single-core, 590.68 in stress-ng single-core, and 16.52 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show average throughput, registering 28297.71 in stress-ng and 7068.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Cryptographic operations perform strongly due to dedicated AES and SHA instruction extensions, scoring 77518.13 in PassMark CPU encryption. In memory subsystems, small-block cached read bandwidth reaches 3743.05 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidth register at 160.37 GB/sec and 79.16 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server maximizes density by combining a substantial 768 GB memory footprint with large direct-attached NVMe storage. Tradeoffs include modest per-core compute output and the absence of AVX-512 instruction extensions. Performance profiles indicate the instance is suited for memory-bound workloads, such as distributed key-value caches like Redis, in-memory databases, big data batch extraction, and large data processing pipelines requiring high-speed local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7571 x86_64 processor. The configuration provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 2.2 GHz, 768 GB of DDR4 memory, 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show modest single-threaded performance offset by average multi-core throughput and strong cryptographic execution via hardware acceleration. Cached memory bandwidth reaches 3743.05 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory operations, while Redis demonstrates 55.8 million SET operations per second. Lacking dedicated GPUs and AVX-512 support, the instance prioritizes memory density and direct NVMe capacity over raw compute velocity. It is suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, ETL pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial RAM and rapid local scratch storage.
